html:
SMTO-FIL-0009 — Invalid regular expression

GUID: 1a2b9300-178c-4705-ac02-5f963b5aa980
Slug: file-invalid-regex
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO tried to search inside files using a text pattern it couldn't run, so the search didn't happen. No files were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, tell SMTO the exact word or phrase you want to find, and ask it to search for that as plain text. A plain-text search avoids the special pattern symbols this search couldn't run.
  2. If you wrote the search pattern yourself, keep it on one line and check that every ( and [ has a matching ) and ]. Patterns that span several lines or have unbalanced brackets are refused before searching.
  3. If you want upper and lower case to match, ask SMTO to ignore case rather than adding (?i) to the pattern. This search refuses settings written inside the pattern but has its own ignore-case option.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's search finishes and shows the matching lines, or tells you nothing matched.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the words you were trying to find, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resend the same pattern unchanged; it will be refused again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway content search rejected a regular expression that spans lines, exceeds 4096 characters, uses an excluded construct (inline flag groups, backtracking verbs, \K/\G/\R/\X, fuzzy matching) or fails to compile.

What this means

  • Search rejected multiline/oversized regular expressions, excluded constructs or patterns that its supported compilers cannot parse. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Search rejected multiline/oversized regular expressions, excluded constructs or patterns that its supported compilers cannot parse.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect pattern length, line breaks and supported regex constructs without converting the query's meaning accidentally.

How to fix it

  • Check the pattern in the receipt (error_kind invalid_regex). Supply a single-line, Python re-compatible expression of at most 4096 characters without mode-changing (?...) groups, verbs or fuzzy syntax, and use the search 'case' argument instead of an inline (?i) flag (gateway_core/file_walk.compile_regex, file_search.search).
  • Correct the search regular expression syntax before searching again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected single-line supported expression compiles and matches the intended sample.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
